newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rates close down on late demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rates close down on late demand.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate extended early falls to close 80 points down at 22 percent on Friday, following late demand for paper from dealers who did not want to stay liquid over the weekend.
"The market was very quiet. Most trade took place in the morning, and overnight rates were stable at around 22.50 percent for most of the session," said a money market trader.
"Nonetheless a late surge in demand by those who had been hanging on to liquidity made us close below session averages," he added.
Traders put the lack of trading activity down to mixed expectations for primary rate trends at next week's government auction.

"Judging by the few trades we've had in the term market, primary rates may be very stable, but there are no clear indications, which means that people prefer to wait and see, and that slows down activity," a trader said.
But analysts thought that 28-day and 91-day Cetes rates may gain slightly at next week's primary auction so as not to make returns less competitive.
Overnight rates on bank paper closed 50 basis points down at 24 percent.
Credit maturities for Monday are estimated at 2.650 billion pesos, but liquidity shortages may be greater due to money being withdrawn from the system prior to the month closing.
